title.narrative: Sustainable land management and restoration of degraded lands mainstreaming biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services in the Southern region of Kazakhstan

Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment [35] 91. Economic benefits [36] will be generated at two levels: the national level and in project areas, where agricultural productivity and livelihoods are threatened by unsustainable practices and environmental degradation. At the national level, the project will support the government to mobilize the finance needed to scale up pasture restoration at scale. This will help increase the overall impact of this and other GEF investments in the country. In project areas, economic benefits for vulnerable farming families will be manifested primarily through the improved livelihoods gained through healthier pastures. In addition, women will be supported in natural resource efficient income-generation and the project will actively support pillar 1 of FAO pillars of decent work agenda (employment creation and enterprise development). 92. Social benefits in project areas include greater food security and nutrition from healthier pastures, both directly and through being able to buy nutritious food with increased incomes. Support to households for socio-economic development is expected to lead to jointly agreed social outcomes and to foster joint decision-making between family members. Income generation will enhance their status, and networking with other entrepreneurial women their self-confidence. The project will support greater resilience of rural women and men vulnerable to land degradation, biodiversity loss and climate change impacts. Enhanced alignment with the VGGT in pasture management planning will also foster social inclusion and cohesion. At the national level, exposure of policymakers to inclusive and pro-restoration tenure models and positive incentives, as well as to dialogue with subnational governments, will lead to more cohesive policy development. [35] Specific guidance on how FAO can promote the Four Pillars of Decent Work in rural areas is provided in the Quick reference for addressing decent rural employment (as well as in the full corresponding Guidance document). For more information on FAO’s work on decent rural employment and related guidance materials please consult the FAO thematic website at: http://www.fao.org/rural-employment/en/. [36] using the terminology and typology in GEF STAP. 2023. Incorporating Co-benefits in the Design of GEF Projects.
